messages:
incident-bot: [P95 LATENCY spike] continuous-batcher queue depth > 10k, KV-cache paging started, several pods reporting CUDA OOM and container restarts. Severity: high. Affected region: us-west-2.

maya: seeing client errors 502/504 from serving gateway and 4 customer incidents opened. Latency > 5s for generator routes.

aj: logs from one runner: 
```
E0901 14:12:31.123 main.cpp:456] CUDAError: out of memory when allocating 312MB
W0901 14:12:31.126 batcher.cpp:789] batch growth: queue_size=12134; kv_memory=78% -> paging
I0901 14:12:31.130 containerd: restart exit_code=137
```

sam: node flaps observed on gpu-node-17, kubelet restarted twice. Kernel oom_kill seen for process pid=2345 (continuous-batcher). Paging on NVME is saturating, I/O latency spiking.

maya: immediate ask: can we drain gpu-node-17 and scale down continuous-batcher concurrency to stop queue pileup? Customer impact: 6 active customers with >1% req failures.

aj: proceeding to scale route config to concurrency=1 and enable fallback-model for heavy routes. Command: `curl -X POST https://console.redwood/api/routes/adjust -d '{"route":"/v1/generate","concurrency":1}'` (will push canary).

deposit-bot: deploy-bot: started canary rollout 42 -> 42a, target=1 instance.

sam: I'll drain node now: `kubectl drain gpu-node-17 --ignore-daemonsets --delete-local-data --force` -> moving pods.

maya: tony, can you notify the 6 customers and mention we're throttling heavy routes and doing node drain?

tony: on it. posting incident update to customers and support channel.

aj: while drain is in progress, temporary mitigation: enable rate-limiter per-tenant and lower batch size. Applying patch to batcher config: 
```
batch_max_size: 8
batch_timeout_ms: 30
kv_cache_eviction_threshold: 0.65
```

maya: after changes, one runner stabilized, no more OOMs on restarted pods. latency trending down to 800-1200ms.

sam: NVME iowait reduced after evicting a large cached shard and restarting pod. Node still marked NotReady for ~2m during drain, but cluster autoscaler kicked another node.

aj: collecting heap traces and KV-cache metrics, capturing core dump from last crash. Will upload to S3: s3://redwood-debug/1769504321/

maya: timeline for postmortem: we need root cause narrowing: why continuous-batcher allowed unbounded growth when kv-cache eviction should have triggered earlier. Also why batcher didn't reject/slow-client.

sam: immediate follow-ups: 1) add hard queue cap with backpressure to gateway; 2) make kv-cache eviction aggressive under paging; 3) add better OOM signaling to orchestrator for graceful request draining.

aj: I'll open a PR with tests to simulate cache paging + batch growth and add a canary for hard-queue-cap.

tony: customers updated: "We throttled heavy routes and drained an affected node; engineering is investigating root cause and will share RCA."

maya: great. incident-bot, please create incident ticket and link runbook.

incident-bot: Created INC-2026-1769504321.runbook -> /incidents/1769504321.

sam: closing notes for oncall handoff: Ongoing work assigned to aj (eng-runtime) and sam (eng-sre). Follow-up meeting scheduled in 2 hours.

maya: handing off to aj for night watch. If latency rises >2s, escalate pager.

aj: ack — I'll monitor the canary and KV metrics for the next 4 hours.

-- end thread --
